subject: general
question: In an election between two candidates, one candidate got 40% of total votes and yet lost by 1000 votes. If all the votes polled were valid, then the total number of votes cast in the election was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total votes be **100%**.

Losing candidate got **40%** → Winning candidate got (100% − 40%) = **60%**.

Difference in votes = 60% − 40% = **20%**.

Given 20% = **1000 votes**.

100% = 1000 ÷ 20 × 100 = **5000 votes**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5000 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/343a879164d7cd106534938849a82a782dee689acdda6d49e656de4fe5479ee3.png] 

**Given:**

Percentage of votes for loser = **40%**

Vote margin (Difference) = **1000**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Votes = 100%

⇒ Votes of winner = 100% − 40% = 60%

⇒ Difference in percentages = 60% − 40% = 20%

⇒ 20% of Total Votes = 1000

⇒ Total Votes = (1000 ÷ 20) × 100

⇒ Total Votes = 50 × 100 = 5000

**∴ The correct answer is 5000 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Invalid Votes Concept

If invalid votes are present, then **Valid Votes** = Total Polled − Invalid. The winning/losing % is then calculated on valid votes unless specified otherwise.

Voter Turnout

If some voters did not cast votes: **Votes Polled** = Total Registered Voters × (Turnout %). Always identify the base population for percentage calculations.</p
